decisions.rationale: "Lesch-Nyhan" names a specific disease but is used adjectivally to modify the noun "patient" ("a Lesch-Nyhan patient"), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines Section 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: "Lesch-Nyhan syndrome" refers to one specific, defined disease with no further categorization.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines Section 1: Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: "Complete deficiency of hypoxanthine guanine phosphoribosyltransferase" names a specific, defined enzyme-deficiency condition (HPRT deficiency) rather than a general term. It parallels the guideline example "C7 deficiency", which is a Specific Disease, and is not the excluded generic use of "deficiency" alone.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines Section 1 (Specific Disease) and Examples item 6 (C7 deficiency); contrast with What NOT to Annotate item 4 (general terms)

decisions.rationale: "Lesch-Nyhan syndrome" is the name of the specific disease of the patient, used as the object of "with" and not as a modifier, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines Section 1: Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: "HPRT deficient" refers to the disease state (HPRT deficiency) but functions as an adjective modifying the noun "patients", so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines Section 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts
